findings.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
findings.summary: On October 21, 2026, Node.js announced the availability of fixes for multiple vulnerabilities across the following supported release lines: 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x. These vulnerabilities impact critical operations such as the Brotli decoder, DNS resolution, and TLS certificate validation. The vulnerabilities pose risks for remote code execution and traffic interception. For more information, see Node.js Security Release . The following vulnerabilities have a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of High and are addressed in this advisory: CVE-2026-111497 - Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write; potential remote code execution CVE-2026-105482 - DNS resolution truncation involving embedded NUL characters CVE-2026-105483 - TLS hostname validation bypass using fullwidth IP digits CVE-2026-106069 - TLS hostname validation bypass with noncanonical IP addresses For information about Splunk products and offerings, including AppDynamics, see Vulnerabilities in Node.js (CVE-2026-111497, CVE-2026-105482, CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069) on Splunk Products - October 2026 This investigation was expanded to cover Brotli outside of Node.js on October 30, 2026. The Brotli decoder flaw (CVE-2026-111497), which is in the Google Brotli C decoder, is often bundled with or linked to other software, so products beyond Node.js may be affected. For software that may be affected, see Broccoli2Shell . Important: If a product is not listed within this advisory, Cisco's review indicates that the product is not affected by these vulnerabilities. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-oct2026-node-js-Jj3SQ19u Security Impact Rating: High CVE: CVE-2026-105482,CVE-2026-105483,CVE-2026-106069,CVE-2026-111497

findings.title: Rapid7 Analysis: VMware vCenter SRP Authentication Bypass to Root (CVE-2026-123890)
findings.summary: Overview An unauthenticated attacker can retrieve the session key for an in-progress administrator login to VMware vCenter's directory service. The attacker then uses that key to complete the login without knowing the account's password. The vulnerable interface is exposed through DCE/RPC on TCP port 2012. The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-123890 , combines a Secure Remote Password (SRP) session-key getter that is callable before authentication with an RPC context lookup that does not enforce ownership. The context handles use predictable UUIDv1 values. By creating two reference contexts around a pending login, an attacker can narrow the hidden login handle to a short timestamp window and ask the server for its key. We reproduced the bypass against vCenter Server Appliance 8.0.2.00400, build 23929136 , running Photon OS 4.0, and leveraged the resulting administrator connection through to root command execution. SSH and Bash access were initially disabled. The attack recovered the directory database and its Security Token Service (STS) signing key, forged an administrator API session, and used appliance administration features to create an account and enable SSH. Neither the existing SSO password nor the root password was an input to that chain. Impact The attacker needs network access to TCP 2012 and the name of an existing SSO principal. Our PoC uses the default SSO administrator principal, administrator@vsphere.local ; deployments using a different SSO domain need the corresponding account name. The attack does not depend on an existing authenticated connection or an administrator being online. The attacker initiates the login attempt in order to recover its session key. The authenticated connection can call the directory database-copy interface. Its raw database contains the STS private signing key, allowing the attacker to sign administrator assertions that vCenter trusts. findings.title: OpenAI, Cisco Unveil Open Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems
findings.summary: OpenAI and Cisco’s Shirudo uses AI-generated shields to block Linux exploits while patches are prepared, but it’s not yet production-ready. The post OpenAI, Cisco Unveil Open Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems appeared first on SecurityWeek .

Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
findings.summary: On November 18, 2026, nginx announced the availability of a fix for multiple critical vulnerabilities in nginx that could lead to remote code execution. These vulnerabilities affect nginx releases 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 and is fixed in releases 1.31.9 (mainline) and 1.30.7 (stable). These vulnerabilities were identified by the following CVEs: CVE-2026-113425: NGINX ngx_mail_proxy_module vulnerability CVE-2026-121810: NGINX ngx_http_v3_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123007: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123633: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123634: NGINX resolver vulnerability For more information, see the nginx Security Advisories . This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-nginx-nov-2026-e8jska2s Security Impact Rating: High CVE: CVE-2026-113425,CVE-2026-121810,CVE-2026-123007,CVE-2026-123633,CVE-2026-123634

findings.title: Vulnerability in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
findings.summary: On November 19, 2026, the PHP Foundation announced the availability of security fixes that address a critical vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution. This vulnerability is identified by CVE-2026-126714. For information about this vulnerability, see the advisory GHSA-fm2m-fjf5-v3cp . This vulnerability is being referenced as phpAfterShell . For information about Splunk products and offerings, see Vulnerabilities in PHP affecting Splunk Products - November 2026 . This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-phpaftershell-nov-2026-kT9pL4Xe Security Impact Rating: Critical CVE: CVE-2026-126714
